content.title: About
content.content: Navel oranges are sweet, juicy citrus fruits derived from the Citrus × sinensis cultivar. Grown in warm regions worldwide, especially the United States, Spain and Italy, they feature a bright orange peel that is easy to remove and are rich in vitamin C, flavonoids, and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “navel” comes from the French word “navelle,” referring to the small belly‑button‑like formation at the blossom end of the fruit.
Navel oranges were first developed in California in the early 20th century.
Juice from navels is generally sweeter and less acidic than juice from other orange varieties.
The peel is frequently used to make zest, marmalade, and aromatic oils.
In the 2020s, navel oranges became the most popular orange variety in the United States.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One medium orange provides over 100 % of the daily recommended vitamin C, which supports immune function and protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as hesperidin have antioxidant properties and may promote cardiovascular health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in oranges helps maintain regular bowel movements and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: May reduce kidney stone risk
items.content: Citrate present in orange juice can help prevent the formation of calcium oxalate stones.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis, contributing to skin elasticity and repair.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oranges, including skin itching, swelling, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Non‑organic oranges may carry pesticide residues on the peel; washing thoroughly before consumption is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Natural sugars in orange juice can raise blood glucose levels; people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Navel oranges can be eaten fresh by segmenting, added to salads, desserts, and smoothies. The peel is used for zest, marmalade, or aromatic spices. Navel orange juice is a popular refreshing drink and a base for sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oranges in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer at 4‑7 °C; they stay fresh for 2‑3 weeks. At room temperature they keep for 5‑7 days. Keep them away from strong‑smelling foods, as the peel readily absorbs odors.
